subject: KaperNova Dedicated onboarding — governance, regional selection & fallback operations
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@kapernova.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@kapernova.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: KaperNova Dedicated onboarding — governance, regional selection & fallback operations

Hi Elena / Samir,

Great to have KaperNova moving to Dedicated — congrats on the decision. I wanted to align on three items before we kick off the implementation sprint next week:

1) Governance and data boundaries — final sign-off on what sits in the private pool vs. hosted backups (we discussed PII isolation for the inference layer).
2) Region choice for primary pool — you flagged US-west and US-east as options; we need to select primary and failover region for compliance and latency.
3) Autoscale & burst policy expectations — baseline steady-state qps, expected peak bursts, and allowable cold-start latency.

Attached is an updated SOW (KaperNova_SOW_v3.pdf) and a short ops checklist. Can you confirm: primary region (us-west/us-east), preferred RTO for fallbacks (30s/120s), and an initial monthly committed throughput? Once we have that we can schedule a 60-minute intake with CS, NetOps and our Dedicated ops lead.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[growth-redwood.ai]
[attachment: KaperNova_SOW_v3.pdf (PDF, 2.1 MB)]

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@kapernova.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@kapernova.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: KaperNova Dedicated onboarding — governance, regional selection & fallback operations

Thanks Grace — quick answers below so we can keep momentum: 

- Primary region: US-East (we have most traffic and a data center in the region).
- Failover: US-West, prefer a warm-failover with RTO ~60s if possible.
- Committed throughput: planning for 1.5M tokens/day initially, with bursts up to 3x for campaign windows.

Elena and I can join the intake next week. Also attaching procurement contact — procurement@kapernova.com — they'll need the final SOW and invoice details.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, KaperNova
[attachment: none]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@kapernova.com>, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@kapernova.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KaperNova Dedicated onboarding — governance, regional selection & fallback operations

Hi Samir / Elena — great, US-East primary with US-West warm-failover and ~1.5M tokens/day baseline is clear. A couple of operational clarifications from the implementation side: 

- Pool topology: we'll propose a 4-GPU pool in US-East (A100/80GB equivalent) with a cold warm-warm cache layer in US-West to meet the 60s RTO.
- Autoscale policy we typically recommend: baseline min instances for steady latency SLAs + burst capacity that scales within 90s for token burst factors up to 3x. If you want faster ramp, that increases committed baseline.
- Network/ingress: NetOps will need CIDR blocks for your egress and the list of third-party integrations that will call the endpoint.

I'm looping in Vivek on NetOps and provisioning timeline — Vivek, can you confirm netops dependencies and whether we can meet a 2-week turn-up after SOW signature?

Thanks,
Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Implementation Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@kapernova.com>, Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@kapernova.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 12:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KaperNova Dedicated onboarding — governance, regional selection & fallback operations

FYI netops checklist and timeline below — extracted from our provisioning playbook. Attaching netops-deps.xlsx with the exact fields we need.

- Prereqs: filled IP allowlist, ASN for BGP (optional), peering request if cross-cloud latency SLA is required.
- Certificates: customer-managed certs allowed; if KaperNova prefers Redwood-managed certs, we need a contact and a CAA approval window.
- Storage/retention: confirm retention window for KV cache and any logs that must be exported to your SIEM.
- Timeline: 10 business days to provision pool once we have signed SOW, CIDRs and a primary point-of-contact for certificate exchange. 3 business days for warm-failover staging in US-West.

Attachments: [attachment: netops-deps.xlsx (XLSX, 85 KB)]

Small ops note: for the 3x burst factor you called out, we recommend a pre-warm policy for scheduled campaigns (we can pre-provision burst capacity for known windows to avoid cold-start penalties). If KaperNova wants pre-warm for marketing pushes, flag those dates in advance.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Engineering Manager, Dedicated Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: KaperNova Dedicated onboarding — governance, regional selection & fallback operations

Hi all — thanks for the quick confirmations. Next concrete steps: 

1) KaperNova to review and sign the attached SOW (KaperNova_SOW_v3.pdf). Procurement, please confirm invoice recipient and PO number so we can generate the DocuSign package.
2) KaperNova to complete netops-deps.xlsx with CIDRs and cert contact (deadline: EOD Thu 2026-06-25 to keep 2-week provisioning).
3) Grace/Monica will schedule the 60-minute intake (CS + Impl + NetOps) for Thu 2026-06-24 or Fri 2026-06-25 — please indicate preferred time windows.

I'll hold a tentative provisioning slot for the week of 2026-07-06 pending signature. If procurement needs a different cadence, let me know and we can adjust.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
